_comment: FIRST EXAMPLE RECIPE — SKELETON (user content, ADR-006). CONFIRMED flow (Session 2): the script does ONLY two things per order — click Close on the popup, then click the clean Accept button that appears on the home screen. Everything else (the actual buy/sell payment: verifying money received, or sending money) the author does MANUALLY on their phone. Targets below are PLACEHOLDERS — fill from a capture (docs/CAPTURE_GUIDE.md + scripts/capture_helper.py).
_workflow: Author's real loop: the phone rings 3x per order (1 assigned / 2 accepted / 3 action-needed). The script auto-Closes + auto-Accepts fast and non-stop. On the 3rd ring the author TOGGLES THE SCRIPT OFF (presses the hotkey), handles that one order on the phone (~6-7 min: swipe/verify for a buy order where money was received, or send money for a sell order), then TOGGLES BACK ON. Pausing while handling an order is what keeps the script from accepting MORE orders than the author can work one at a time — the toggle is the whole point.
_mode: AUTO-ACCEPT, fast. No inter-click delays (author wants it ultrafast); wait_for still guards each click so we never click a not-yet-rendered element. Revert to close-only = delete the final 'click Accept' step.
_placeholders_todo: Replace text:'Close' and text:'Accept' with the real targets from capture (add css_selector/xpath; note the frame — main vs iframe). If a bare 'Close' can appear on non-order modals, make it more specific so the script only closes real order popups.
